name: Battery & Master Cutoff
description: Battery, battery box and hold-down, terminals and lugs, the master electrical cutoff (mechanical 4-post switch or solid-state isolator), internal and external kill switches, alternator field-kill / dump resistor and the main fuse. The Gen 6 Camaro carries its factory battery in the trunk on the right side; this build keeps the battery in the rear (right side, low, ahead of or over the rear axle line) and runs the main cable forward through the cabin.

components.name: Battery
components.description: 12 V starting/service battery. Factory Gen 6 cars use an AGM battery in the trunk (OE size changed from H7 to H6 / Group 48 for 2016). For a race car, a compact AGM (Odyssey PC925/PC680) or a LiFePO4 race battery saves 10–19 kg. Size it for cranking a high-compression 6.2 L LT (hot restart is the hard case) plus key-off draws from the ECU, logger and transponder.
components.location: Trunk, right (passenger) side, low on the floor in a sealed box, in the factory battery area (rear quarter). Keep it inside the cage perimeter and away from the fuel cell; some builders move it to the passenger rear floor area behind the seat for polar-moment reasons.

factory.name: ACDelco Professional AGM, Group H6 / 48 (2016+ Gen 6, trunk mounted)
factory.notes: Optima reports the OE size changed from H7 (2015) to H6 for 2016. Group H6/48 AGM ~ 760–840 CCA, ~21–22 kg. Factory battery has a vent tube to the outside because it lives in the trunk; keep it if retaining an OE flooded/AGM battery inside the car.

raceOptions.name: Odyssey PC925 / ODS-AGM28L
raceOptions.notes: 480 CCA, 10.8 kg, 168 x 175 x 127 mm, M6 receptacle terminals, max terminal torque 60 in-lb (6.8 N·m). Most common road-race choice for a V8: sealed AGM, mount in any orientation except inverted.

raceOptions.name: Odyssey PC680 / ODS-AGM16L
raceOptions.notes: 280 CCA, 7.0 kg. Marginal for a hot 6.2 L restart; only with a lightweight gear-reduction starter and good cables.

raceOptions.name: Antigravity ATX30-RS Re-Start (LiFePO4)
raceOptions.notes: 880 CA (lead-acid-equivalent rating), 2.6 kg, 16 Ah actual, 165 x 127 x 173 mm. Built-in BMS and Re-Start reserve. Manufacturer lists automotive use as 'race only' by enquiry. Needs a charging voltage the BMS accepts (~14.2–14.6 V) – set alternator/ECM charge target accordingly.

raceOptions.name: Odyssey PC1200
raceOptions.notes: 725 CCA, 17.3 kg, SAE posts. Choose for endurance racing with lights, cool-suit and fans running for hours.

specs.Nominal voltage: 12 V (AGM 12.8 V rest), LiFePO4 13.2 V rest
specs.Min cranking capability (recommended): ≥ 450 CCA for a 6.2 L LT with OE starter (estimate)
specs.Location: Trunk right side (factory area) in sealed box

hardware.item: Odyssey PC925 M6 terminal bolt (into M6 receptacle)
hardware.spec: M6 x 1.0 stainless bolt with lock washer, length to suit lug + adaptor
hardware.notes: Over-torquing pulls the brass insert out of the case. Odyssey M6-to-SAE post adaptors are available if SAE clamps are preferred.
Only if the PC680 is used.

hardware.notes: Typical GM battery clamp value; confirm in GM SI for your model year.

hardware.item: Terminal protector boots (positive red, negative black)
hardware.notes: Positive terminal must be fully insulated (SCCA/NASA tech check point).

hardware.spec: NO-OX-ID or dielectric grease, thin film after tightening

installNotes: Build and weld/bolt the battery box mount to the trunk floor before paint (phase 1) so the battery sits low and inside the cage.
Fit the battery with all switches OFF; connect the positive (isolated) side first and the negative last.
Torque terminals to the battery maker's limit (PC925: 60 in-lb) – these are much lower than typical lug torques.
Charge the battery fully on a smart charger with the correct profile (AGM vs Lithium) before first start.
If using a LiFePO4 battery, confirm the ECM/alternator charge target and that the BMS will not cut off during cranking.
inspection: Resting voltage after the car sits overnight with master OFF (AGM ≥ 12.7 V, LiFePO4 ≥ 13.2 V).
Terminal tightness and corrosion; case cracks/bulging.
Hold-down tight – the battery must not move with a firm push.

components.name: Battery box & hold-down
components.description: Sealed, vented battery box with a positive mechanical hold-down. Rules (SCCA GCR, NASA CCR) require a battery in the driver/passenger compartment to be in a non-conductive marine-type box or sealed enclosure and secured with bolts (no bungees/zip ties). The box also contains acid if a flooded battery is used.
components.location: Trunk floor, right side; bolted through the floor with backing plates.

factory.notes: OE tray + J-bolt/retainer clamp; vent tube exits through the floor.

raceOptions.brand: Various (e.g. Moroso, Longacre, Kirkey, Odyssey-sized billet trays)
raceOptions.notes: Billet/fabricated tray with bar clamp and two 1/4 in or M8 threaded rods; add a lid if mounted in the cabin.

raceOptions.name: Sealed marine-style plastic box
raceOptions.notes: Non-conductive, meets 'sealed box' rules for cabin mounting; vent tube to outside if not an AGM.

hardware.spec: M8 x 1.25 (or 5/16-18) flange bolt + large backing plate/washer under floor
hardware.notes: Use 50 mm x 3 mm steel backing plates under thin trunk-floor sheetmetal. Rules typically require at least 2 bolts of 5/16 in (8 mm) minimum for hold-downs.

hardware.spec: 1/4-20 or M8 rod with nyloc nut
hardware.torque: 5–7 ft-lb (7–10 N·m) – snug; do not crack case

hardware.notes: Typical GM value for battery hold-down; confirm in GM SI.

hardware.spec: 3/8 in ID PVC vent tube with floor grommet

installNotes: Position the box so the cable exits face the cable route forward (right-side rocker) and so the box clears the fuel cell and its vent/fill hoses.
Drill, deburr, and paint holes; seal with seam sealer around backing plates.
Install rubber pad under the battery to reduce vibration.
inspection: Check bolts and clamp tightness each event.

components.name: Solid-state battery isolator (electronic master switch)
components.description: Electronic FIA-style master switch that isolates the battery negative and simultaneously sends an engine-kill signal to the ECU/PDM, with internal and external push buttons. Eliminates running heavy cables to a mechanical switch on the dash – very attractive on a Gen 6 with the battery in the trunk. Must be confirmed legal with your sanctioning body; some club tech inspectors only accept mechanical switches.
components.location: Bolted directly on/next to the battery negative terminal in the trunk box.

raceOptions.name: Cartek Battery Isolator XR
raceOptions.notes: Negative-side isolation, 550–650 A typical / 2000 A surge, 7–18 V, M8 battery stud, engine-kill output 12 V @ 0.5 A (signal to ECU/PDM). 'Suitable up to standard V8'. Datasheet Feb 2023.

raceOptions.name: Cartek Battery Isolator GT
raceOptions.notes: Higher-spec version with built-in alternator run-down (no dump resistor needed) and up to 40 A engine-kill output that can directly power an ECU/ignition circuit.

specs.Kill output: 12 V 0.5 A on, grounded when off (XR)

hardware.item: Battery negative stud nut (isolator body to battery lug)
hardware.notes: Cartek datasheet gives M8 stud; torque value not published – estimate for an M8 brass stud.

hardware.spec: Tinned copper lug, 1/0–2 AWG, M8 hole, adhesive-lined heat shrink

installNotes: Mount the isolator on the battery negative; everything else (alternator, PDM, starter) is on the vehicle side.
Wire the engine-kill output to the ECU/PDM kill input so the engine stops even with the alternator charging.
Wire internal (driver) and external buttons; test both with engine running before first track day.
Confirm legality with the series tech director before purchase.
inspection: Function test both kill buttons with engine idling every event.
Check the status LED / fault indication.

components.name: Mechanical master electrical cutoff switch (4-post)
components.description: Rotary master switch in the main battery positive cable with a second, lower-current pole that kills the alternator/ignition so the engine stops when the switch is turned off. SCCA wording requires it to be in a battery cable and cut all electrical circuits except an onboard fire system; NASA allows life-support/radio exceptions. Use a high-amperage race switch – cheap 50 A switches fail under starter current.
components.location: Dash center/lower console within reach of the belted driver (x≈1.15, y≈0.62, z≈0.05), or near the rear on the main cable with a pull-cable to the exterior.

raceOptions.name: Longacre weatherproof 4-terminal disconnect
raceOptions.notes: Sealed back; alternator circuit rated 125 A – matches high-output OE alternators.

raceOptions.name: Longacre 4-terminal with panel
raceOptions.notes: Includes aluminum panel; 20 A alternator/ignition pole.

raceOptions.name: Longacre 2-terminal disconnect
raceOptions.notes: 175 A continuous, 1000 A peak, 3/8 in studs; no alternator pole – only usable with a separate field-kill relay/dump resistor.

raceOptions.name: FIA 6-pole master switch with resistor
raceOptions.notes: European-style switch with built-in resistor to prevent engine run-on from the alternator after switch-off.

hardware.item: Main stud nuts (battery in / load out)
hardware.notes: Hold the inner nut with a wrench while torquing the outer nut so the stud does not spin inside the switch body.

hardware.spec: Rubber boot or fabricated Lexan cover over live studs

installNotes: Plan the cable route: battery (trunk) → master switch → starter/front junction. With a trunk battery the switch is commonly mounted on the rear package tray/near the battery with a pull cable to the outside, or on the dash with both heavy cables routed through the cabin.
Wire the auxiliary pole to break the alternator output (via dump resistor) or ECM ignition/run feed so the engine dies when switched off.
Mark ON/OFF clearly on the panel.
Test: engine idling at 2000 rpm, turn switch off – engine must stop within ~1 s.
inspection: Check studs for heat discoloration (sign of loose lug).
Check switch action and key/handle retention.

components.name: Alternator field-kill relay / dump resistor
components.description: When the master switch opens with the engine running, the alternator can keep the ignition/ECU alive (engine run-on) and voltage can spike. A power resistor across the alternator output (switched in by the master switch's aux pole) or a field-kill relay that drops the alternator L/field terminal ensures the engine stops. With the Gen V LT ECM-controlled alternator, killing the ECM run feed also drops the L-terminal command.
components.location: Near the master switch or on the firewall, on a heat-tolerant aluminum mount.

raceOptions.name: FIA master switch with integrated resistor
raceOptions.notes: Resistor pole is built into 6-pole FIA switches.

raceOptions.name: Cartek Isolator GT (alternator run-down function)
raceOptions.notes: Electronic alternator run-down replaces the resistor.

installNotes: Mount on bare metal for heat sinking; insulate the terminals.
Verify run-on does not occur with lights and fans off (lowest load case).

modelRef.features: Gold anodised finned aluminium housing, 4 mounting tabs, 2 solder lugs.

components.name: External master switch actuator (pull cable or push button)
components.description: Exterior-accessible actuator so corner workers can kill the car. SCCA closed-car wording places it in front of the windshield on the cowl or top of fender (driver side) close enough to reach if overturned, or below the center of the rear window. Marked with the international spark-in-blue-triangle decal (minimum ~12 cm base).
components.location: Driver-side cowl at the base of the windshield (x≈0.66, y≈0.98, z≈+0.45), or rear-window base center.

raceOptions.name: Pull cable with T-handle (for mechanical switch)
raceOptions.notes: Cable must pull the switch to OFF; route with gentle bends and secure every 300 mm.

raceOptions.name: Remote push button for electronic isolator
raceOptions.notes: Supplied with the isolator kits; sealed red button.

specs.Marking: Red spark on white-edged blue triangle decal, 'OFF' direction marked

hardware.spec: 3/16 in stainless rivets or M5 screws with nyloc

installNotes: Mount after body panels are fitted (phase 10) but run the cable/harness in phase 8.
Test from outside the car with the window net up.
inspection: Pull/press test each event; check decal present.

components.name: Main fuse / mega-fuse holder (PDM & accessory feed)
components.description: High-current fuse protecting the long cable run from battery to PDM/front. The starter circuit is normally left unfused (cranking current) but the branch feeding the PDM and aux block must be fused close to the source. Use a MEGA/ANL or a resettable high-current breaker.
components.location: In the trunk next to the battery/isolator (feeds the main cable) and/or at the front power junction where the PDM feed branches.
